posts.title: 17 hours awake can impair you like a drink
posts.caption: After 17-19 hours awake, performance dropped to the level seen at 0.05% blood alcohol in one well-known study (Williamson & Feyer, 2000). Protect your sleep. #sleep #sleepscience #healthtok #sleeptips #sleepscore

slides.text: 17 hours awake and your brain performs like you've had a drink
slides.sub: What sleep loss does to you

slides.label: The research
slides.title: After 17–19 hours awake, performance matched 0.05% blood alcohol
slides.body: In a widely cited study, reaction time and accuracy on tests dropped to the level seen at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05%.
slides.source: Source: Williamson & Feyer, Occup Environ Med, 2000

slides.label: Go further
slides.title: At 24 hours awake it was around 0.10%
slides.body: That is above the 0.08% US legal driving limit. Being awake a full day is not a small thing.

slides.label: The trap
slides.title: People tend to underestimate how impaired they are
slides.body: Attention, reaction time, and judgement slip first, and those are the skills you use to notice that you're slipping.

slides.label: What helps
slides.title: Protect a consistent wake time
slides.body: Get light in your first hour awake and keep caffeine earlier in the day. Small habits that support better sleep.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.

posts.title: 5 things that can raise your sleep score
posts.caption: Five habits that tend to support better sleep and a better sleep score. Pick one and run it for a week. #sleepscore #sleeptips #sleep #sleephygiene #healthtok

slides.text: 5 things that can raise your sleep score

slides.title: Wake at the same time every day
slides.body: Even weekends. A steady wake time helps anchor your body clock, and regular sleep is linked to better sleep quality.

slides.title: Get morning light
slides.body: A few minutes to half an hour outside in your first hour awake helps set your body clock for the night ahead.

slides.title: Cool and dark
slides.body: Around 65°F (18°C) and as dark as you can make it. Blackout curtains or a mask both work.

slides.title: Set a caffeine cutoff
slides.body: Many experts suggest stopping 8 or more hours before bed. Caffeine can cut sleep even 6 hours out.

slides.title: Wind down for 30 minutes
slides.body: Dim the lights and do something calm. Give your brain a runway instead of a cliff.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.

posts.title: Your sleep score is not a medical number
posts.caption: Wearable sleep scores are estimates, not a sleep lab. Trends over weeks are more useful than any single night. #sleepscore #sleep #sleepscience #wearables #healthtok

slides.text: Your sleep score is not a medical number
slides.sub: Here is how to use it anyway

slides.label: What it is
slides.title: An estimate from movement and heart rate
slides.body: Most wearables model your sleep. A sleep lab measures brain activity directly, and that is the gold standard.

slides.label: Why trends win
slides.title: One bad night means very little
slides.body: Look at your two-week average. Trends show what your habits are doing, and single nights are mostly noise.

slides.label: What moves it
slides.title: Duration, consistency, and a calmer night
slides.body: Alcohol and late heavy meals tend to raise nighttime heart rate, which tends to pull scores down.

slides.label: How to use it
slides.title: Change one habit, watch the trend
slides.body: Pick one change for a week: caffeine cutoff, wake time, or room temperature. Then compare.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.

posts.title: Why do you wake up tired after 8 hours?
posts.caption: Hours are only part of the story. Timing, sleep quality, and sometimes a sleep disorder matter too. If you're tired every day, talk to a doctor. #sleep #sleeptips #sleepscience #healthtok #tired

slides.text: Why do you wake up tired after 8 hours?

slides.title: Your schedule is inconsistent
slides.body: Shifting sleep by a couple of hours on weekends is sometimes called social jet lag, and it can leave you groggy on Monday.

slides.title: Sleep inertia
slides.body: Waking from deep sleep can cause grogginess that typically fades within about 30 minutes. Light and movement help.

slides.title: Quality, not just quantity
slides.body: Alcohol, noise, light, and heat can fragment sleep so 8 hours in bed is less than 8 hours of good sleep.

slides.title: Something medical
slides.body: If you are tired every day despite enough time in bed, ask a doctor. Sleep apnea is common and often missed.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.

posts.title: Coffee 6 hours before bed cost over an hour of sleep
posts.caption: Caffeine is linked to less sleep even when taken 6 hours before bed (Drake et al., J Clin Sleep Med, 2013). Try an earlier cutoff for a week and see what your sleep trend does. #sleep #sleeptips #sleepscore #caffeine #healthtok

slides.text: Coffee 6 hours before bed cost people over an hour of sleep
slides.sub: One study, and what to do about it

slides.label: The study
slides.title: Caffeine 6 hours before bed still cost over an hour of sleep
slides.body: Researchers gave people 400 mg of caffeine 0, 3, or 6 hours before bedtime. Even the 6-hour group slept over an hour less.
slides.source: Source: Drake et al., J Clin Sleep Med, 2013

slides.label: The catch
slides.title: You may not notice it
slides.body: Participants did not always feel that their sleep was worse. The effect can be there even when you feel fine.

slides.label: The dose
slides.title: 400 mg is about four cups of coffee
slides.body: Smaller amounts have smaller effects, but timing still matters. Sensitivity varies a lot from person to person.

slides.label: Try this
slides.title: Set a caffeine cutoff at least 8 hours before bed
slides.body: Bed at 11 pm? Last coffee around 3 pm. Give it a week and watch your sleep score trend.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.

posts.title: Sleep is the most underrated performance upgrade
posts.caption: Memory, mood, immunity, and safety all lean on sleep. Most adults need 7 or more hours. #sleep #sleepscience #healthtok #sleeptips #sleepscore

slides.text: Sleep is the most underrated performance upgrade
slides.sub: It's free. Here's what it does.

slides.label: Memory
slides.title: Sleep helps lock in what you learned
slides.body: While you sleep, your brain consolidates memories from the day. Cutting sleep short cuts that process.

slides.label: Mood
slides.title: Short sleep is linked to lower mood and higher stress
slides.body: When you're underslept, small problems tend to feel bigger.

slides.label: Immunity
slides.title: Short sleepers caught more colds
slides.body: In one study, people sleeping under 6 hours had roughly four times the odds of catching a cold after virus exposure versus 7+ hours.

slides.label: Safety
slides.title: Reaction time and accuracy drop with less sleep
slides.body: That is why fatigue is a factor in many accidents, from driving to the workplace.

slides.label: How much
slides.title: Most adults need 7 or more hours
slides.body: That is the consensus recommendation from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and the Sleep Research Society.

slides.text: Better sleep is a skill. Get one tip a day.
